# The Right Way to Import JavaScript in Laravel Blade Templates A common stumbling block when building Laravel applications involves ensuring client-side scripts execute correctly within Blade templates. Developers often encounter scenarios where a script tag appears correct, the asset path resolves accurately, yet the expected functions remain undefined. This usually points to a misunderstanding of how HTML loading order interacts with JavaScript execution, or a mismatch between ES6 module syntax and legacy browser support. Consider a typical setup where an `index.blade.php` view extends a layout and attempts to load a custom script via ``. The logic here seems sound: the URL resolves to `/js/components/pizza.js`, which exists in the public directory. However, if that file contains an `import` statement at the top level, such as `import PizzaService from '../services/PizzaService.js';`, you will likely face a `ReferenceError` when trying to call functions defined in that script. The root cause is often twofold. First, modern JavaScript files using ES6 modules cannot be loaded into standard HTML ` @stack('scripts') ``` Then, in your specific view (`index.blade.php`), push the script into that stack using `@push`. ```blade @section('content')
@endsection @push('scripts') @endpush ``` This method ensures that your custom scripts load after all core framework assets, preventing issues where DOM elements or jQuery are accessed before they exist. However, if your script relies on ES6 imports, you must ensure the browser environment supports modules. If you encounter `SyntaxError: import declarations may only appear at top level of a module`, it often indicates that the browser is treating the file as a standard script despite the syntax used.
